I manage maintenance at a bottling plant with twelve filling lines. Each line logs temperature, vibration and pressure every minute. When a line stops unexpectedly we lose half a shift. Right now we only fix things after they fail. I'd like a warning a day or two before a line is likely to go down, so we can plan the repair during a quiet hour.

We are a small NGO that gives micro-loans to women running home businesses. Over five years we've collected application forms and repayment histories. Our field officers decide by feeling, and it's uneven between regions. We want something that looks at a new application and gives a sense of whether the loan will be repaid on time. It must be fair and easy to explain to the officers.

Our online language school sells yearly subscriptions. About a month before the renewal date, our team has time to reach maybe a hundred students. We have their lesson attendance, quiz scores and logins. The question is who to call first: the ones who otherwise won't renew. Can you set that up?

I run the volunteer program for a food bank. We have sign-up and shift records for three years. Lately it feels like fewer people come back after their first shift, but I don't have numbers. I'd like to see how many volunteers return for a second shift, how this changed by year, and whether it differs by the site they started at. Nothing fancy, just the facts from what we have.

We are a mid-size bank with a network of branches. Each account holder has products, balances and transaction counts. Marketing keeps talking about 'the young savers' and 'the business owners' but nobody has checked. Please look at our current customers and find natural groups among them, with a short description of each group and how big it is. We will use it to plan campaigns later.

Our logistics firm moved to new routing software in March. I'd like to compare the average delivery time, the share of late deliveries and the fuel cost per route for the three months before and the three months after the switch. Please break it down by depot. I just need the comparison laid out clearly.

I'm the admin of a small chain of pharmacies. Every pharmacy sends me its weekly sales as a spreadsheet, but each one uses different column names and some put totals at the bottom. Each Monday I spend hours copying them together. I'd like one clean combined table with the same columns, without the total rows, and the pharmacy name added to each row.

We're moving our school's student records into a new system. The old export has full names in one column, birth dates written in several ways, and missing class codes for some kids. The new system wants first and last name separately, dates as year-month-day, and every student with a class. Can you prepare the file for the import and show me which records you couldn't fix?

Our sensors write a reading every few seconds, but sometimes skip minutes or send the same reading twice. Before anyone can study it, I'd like the readings turned into one row per sensor per minute. Gaps should be marked clearly rather than invented. The result should go into a file the engineers can open.

I'm the operations lead at a regional courier company. Each morning the depot managers ask me how yesterday went: parcels delivered, failed attempts, late vans. I pull this from three systems and paste it into a slide. I'd like a page they can open themselves that is current every morning, with each depot side by side, so they can decide where to send extra drivers.

Our school district reports attendance to the education office every month. The numbers come from each school's register, and someone in each school types them into a template. It takes days and there are errors. We want a monthly attendance report per school and grade that is produced the same way every time and can be sent to the office.

We run a mobile app with a subscription. The founders look at signups, active users, paid conversions and refunds in a weekly meeting. Right now someone exports numbers from four tools every Sunday night. We want one place with these numbers, kept current, broken down by platform and country.
